key_insight: Adaptivity closes the stabilizer-learning sample-complexity gap: with only single-copy Clifford measurements, an optimal algorithm learns any n-qubit stabilizer state in Θ(n) copies.
engineering_relevance: This enables resource-efficient quantum state verification and learning protocols for benchmarking, error-correction workflows, and near-term devices where multi-copy Bell measurements are impractical.
method: Use adaptive single-copy Clifford measurements instead of two-copy Bell measurements.
Update each measurement choice based on previous outcomes to recover the stabilizer structure in polynomial time.
Extend the same adaptive strategy to tolerant testing and to low-nullity states with bounded T-gate content.
evidence_signal: From the abstract, the method matches the optimal Θ(n) copy complexity for exact stabilizer learning and achieves the stated testing tradeoff Θ(n-k+1/ε) with k qubits of quantum memory.
watch_item: Performance and robustness will depend on adaptive control accuracy and measurement noise, which may complicate implementation on hardware.
paper_title: Adaptivity is all you need: Optimal stabilizer learning using just single-copy measurements
